reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the cap is limited to amounts 'ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO ... FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO', which is materially narrower than the fallback's 12 months' fees and can fall below six months' fees, and the only carve-out is Section 8 — confidentiality (Section 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap, failing the fallback carve-out list.

Redline is valid and directionally correct for the customer: it keeps the cap mutual, changes the basis to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, measures from the event giving rise to liability, and adds a single 'Excluded Claims' sentence covering Section 8 indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud, consistent with the model language and redline guidance.

The mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion was left intact, so the edit does not disturb terms that already comply; the high changed-character ratio (0.698) is explained by the required change of cap basis plus insertion of the carve-out definition, not gratuitous rewriting.

Comment is accurate on the substance and cites the playbook position, though 'confirmed that ... sit outside the cap' understates that confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud were newly added as carve-outs — minor wording nit only.
Open item correctly disclosed: the apparent duplicate at p0092 must be conformed to the edited p0090, otherwise the original transaction-limited cap could survive in the executed text.
